key_insight: COVID-19 vaccination was associated with better overall survival among cancer patients in Northwestern Russia; this was not an AI drug discovery study.
clinical_relevance: The findings highlight low vaccination coverage and an association with survival in cancer patients, without establishing causality.
method: Linked cancer registry, vaccination records, and AI-analyzed chest CT data for 1,144 patients.
Compared survival using Kaplan–Meier and adjusted Cox regression analyses.
Used March and November 2021 landmark analyses to mitigate immortal time bias.
evidence_signal: Only 6.6% received vaccination; the primary landmark analysis reported 3-year survival of 80.3% versus 45.7% and an adjusted mortality hazard ratio of 0.40 (95% CI 0.25–0.64).
watch_item: Vaccinated patients had earlier-stage cancer and less active treatment, so residual confounding may partly explain the survival association despite adjustment.
paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
